lp.hero.title: See what your competitors changed this week.
lp.hero.lede: Sparton finds the shops you compete with, reads their whole catalogue, and tells you every Sunday who moved a price, ran a sale or sold out. Each number links to the page it came from.
lp.hero.fine: Free for 1 shop and 3 competitors. Shopify, WooCommerce and Lightspeed.

lp.story.title: How Sparton works
lp.s1.title: You give us one thing: your shop's address.
lp.s1.body: From your address Sparton works out what you sell, so it can go looking for the shops that sell the same.
lp.s2.title: It finds the shops you actually compete with.
lp.s2.body: No list of URLs to paste. Sparton suggests shops that sell what you sell, and you confirm the ones that matter. Nobody is watched until you say so.
lp.s3.title: It reads every product they sell.
lp.s3.body: Names, prices, sale prices and stock, for the whole catalogue. On Shopify and WooCommerce it comes from the shop's own product feed, exact to the cent.
lp.s4.title: Then it watches. Every move lands on the board.
lp.s4.body: Price cuts, price rises, sales with their "was" price, products that sell out or come back, and new products. Weekly on Free, daily on Pro, twice a day on Business.
lp.s5.title: And it tells you how sure it is.
lp.s5.body: Where a shop publishes its own product data, the number is exact and the tile is solid. Where Sparton has to read the page, the tile is hatched and the row says "extracted". You always know which is which.
lp.s6.title: On Sunday you get the week in plain language.
lp.s6.body: A short report of what changed and what it means for you. The numbers come from the comparison, never from the AI; the AI only writes the sentences, and every claim links to its evidence.
lp.plans.title: Plans
lp.plans.lede: Start free. Upgrade when it earns its keep. Prices exclude VAT; cancel any time from the dashboard.
lp.faq.title: Questions
lp.faq.a1: Sparton only reads pages a shop has made public, identifies itself honestly, respects robots.txt and waits between requests. It never logs in, never bypasses anything and never touches a checkout.
lp.faq.a2: On Shopify and WooCommerce shops Sparton reads the shop's own product feed: the price to the cent, including the "was" price of a sale and whether it is in stock. Where a shop publishes no feed, Sparton reads the product data the shop puts in its own pages (schema.org), which counts as exact too. Only as a last resort does it extract the price from the page itself; those rows are labelled "extracted".
lp.faq.q3: Does the AI make up numbers?
lp.faq.a3: No. Every number comes from comparing two readings of the same product. The AI only writes the sentences around those facts and may use no figure that is not in them. If the AI is unavailable you still get a correct report, just a plainer one.
lp.faq.a4: Weekly on Free, daily on Pro and twice a day on Business. The first check of a new competitor sets the baseline; changes appear from the second check on.
lp.faq.a5: Any webshop with public product pages. Shopify and WooCommerce shops give exact data through their feeds; other platforms, Lightspeed included, are read from the product data on the page and labelled accordingly.
lp.faq.a6: Any time, from the dashboard. No email, no call. You keep access until the end of the period you paid for.
lp.faq.q7: What happens to my data if I leave?
lp.faq.a7: You can delete your account at any time, which removes your shops, competitors, readings and reports.
lp.close.title: Next Sunday, know what moved.

vs.metaTitle: Sparton vs Prisync: the facts, with sources
vs.title: Sparton vs Prisync
vs.lede: Both watch competitor prices. They are built for different shops. Here are the facts side by side; every Prisync figure links to Prisync's own pricing page, so you can check it.
vs.date: Prisync facts read from prisync.com/pricing on 1 October 2026. Prices change; check the source before you decide.
vs.r1.them: $99 per month (Professional, 100 products), after a 14-day free trial without a card.
vs.r2.us: Shops and competitors. Every product a competitor sells is read.
vs.r2.them: Products: 100, 1,000 or 5,000 per plan, with unlimited competitors.
vs.r3.us: Sparton suggests shops that sell what you sell; you confirm the ones to watch. No URLs to paste.
vs.r3.them: URL-based plans: you add competitor URLs one by one or in bulk, per product. Channel-based plans track the competitors on your sales channels, from $199 per month.
vs.r4.us: Weekly on Free, daily on Pro, twice a day on Business.
vs.r4.them: Three times a day on URL-based plans; daily on channel-based plans.
vs.r5.them: Available from Premium, charged at an extra 20% on top of the monthly fee.
vs.r7.us: Labelled per competitor: exact when read from the shop's own feed, "extracted" when read from the page.
vs.r7.them: Not stated on the pricing page, so not compared here.
vs.fit.us1: you run one to a few small webshops in the Netherlands or Belgium;
vs.fit.us2: you'd rather confirm suggested competitors than collect URLs per product;
vs.fit.us3: a weekly report in plain language, with the evidence linked, is what you will actually read.
vs.fit.them1: you track a large catalogue against a set list of competitor product pages;
vs.fit.them2: you need prices checked several times a day on every plan;
vs.fit.them3: you want to track competitors across marketplaces and sales channels.
vs.close: Try it on your own shop, free.
vs.footer: Prisync is a trademark of its owner. Sparton is not affiliated with Prisync.
